title: The Best Team of at Most k Engineers

concept.title: Fix the weakest member by sorting; keep the k fastest of the stronger ones in a min-heap
body: Engineer `i` has a speed and an efficiency. The *performance* of a team is **(the sum of the speeds) times (the smallest efficiency in the team)**. Choose a team of **at most `k`** engineers with the largest performance.

Two quantities pull in different directions, so fix one. Sort the engineers by **efficiency, from high to low**. When the engineers are processed in this order, the engineer being processed has the **smallest efficiency among all engineers seen so far**, so if he is in the team, the minimum efficiency of the team is his. Now we only have to choose the best other members from those seen so far: the ones with the **largest speeds**, at most `k` in total.

A **min-heap of speeds** keeps the best (at most) `k` speeds seen so far: push the new speed and add it to a running sum; when the heap holds more than `k` speeds, remove the smallest one and subtract it from the sum. After each engineer, the candidate performance is `sum * (his efficiency)`.

body.code:
team = sorted(zip(eff, speed), reverse=True)     # high efficiency first
heap, total, best = [], 0, 0
for e, s in team:
    heappush(heap, s)
    total += s
    if len(heap) > k:
        total -= heappop(heap)                  # drop the slowest
    best = max(best, total * e)                 # e is the smallest efficiency so far

body: Is the candidate valid when the current engineer was himself dropped as the slowest? Then the real team has a larger minimum efficiency and a sum at least as large, so the true value is even better and was or will be seen at another step; the maximum is not harmed. The largest result is about 2 * 10^9 * 10^9 = 2 * 10^18, which fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

statement: `n` engineers have a speed and an efficiency. The performance of a team is the sum of the speeds of its members multiplied by the smallest efficiency among its members. Choose a team of at least one and at most `k` engineers. Print the largest possible performance.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers: the speed of each engineer.
The third line has `n` numbers: the efficiency of each engineer.

examples.note: The engineers with the speeds 10 and 5 and efficiencies 4 and 7 form a team: (10 + 5) * min(4, 7) = 60.

hints: Sort the engineers by efficiency from high to low: the current one then has the smallest efficiency so far.
Keep the k largest speeds seen so far in a min-heap and their sum.
After each engineer, the candidate is sum * his efficiency; take the maximum over all.

explanation: Engineers are processed by decreasing efficiency, so the current one has the smallest efficiency so far. A min-heap keeps the k largest speeds and their sum; after each engineer, sum * efficiency is a candidate, and the largest candidate is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
speed = list(map(int, input().split()))
eff = list(map(int, input().split()))

import heapq
team = sorted(zip(eff, speed), reverse=True)
heap = []
total = 0
best = 0
for e, s in team:
    heapq.heappush(heap, s)
    total += s
    if len(heap) > k:
        total -= heapq.heappop(heap)
    best = max(best, total * e)
print(best)
